source.title: LLMs Meet Finance: Fine-Tuning Foundation Models for the Open FinLLM Leaderboard
source.authors: V. Rao; Youran Sun; Mahendra Kumar; Tejas Mutneja; Agastya Mukherjee; Hai-Zhao Yang

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present. The scaling-law equation is imperfectly rendered in the extracted text, so its exponent is recorded without inferring a missing sign or intercept.
record.tranche_reason: Tests data scaling in a new setting: financial-task fine-tuning, using average F1 rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a data-fraction scaling result for financial fine-tuning. Its SFT, DPO, and synthetic-data results are not scaling measurements and are not included as rows. The individual average F1 values are shown in Figure 2 but are not stated numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: The authors fine-tune on 12.5–100% of the aggregated financial data and fit a power law of downstream error (1−F1) against data fraction. This is a new setting (fine-tuning, downstream F1) with its own result on scaling form. It bears on V5 (fine-tuning regime) and V6 (downstream performance vs data scale).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors fit log(1−F1) = −0.28 log(d) + const on financial tasks. They compare it with 0.24, which they derive by combining Kaplan's loss exponents with Wu et al.'s inference-scaling error exponent. They claim the consistency suggests a universal, task-independent critical exponent.
record.recipe_differences: Measures average F1/error scaling with data quantity during financial-task fine-tuning, rather than held-out pretraining loss across model, token, or compute scales.
record.problems: The scaling experiment does not identify the model or its size. Individual F1 values appear only in a figure, and no uncertainty estimates are stated. The extracted equation is imperfectly rendered.
record.rows_left_out: SFT, DPO, and synthetic-data results in Tables I–III were left out because they do not measure scaling with model, data, or compute size.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute is not measured.
No extrapolation from small to much larger runs is tested.
Only fine-tuning-data scaling, on one unidentified ~1.5B model, over <1 order of magnitude. No other modalities, repeated data or transfer.
No scaling with model size or pretraining loss. Predictive accuracy of the fit is not tested on held-out larger data sizes.
Fitting choices and setup are not varied.

missing.what: Per-fraction average F1 values (four points) are shown only in the figure and not tabulated. Approximate readings would let researchers check fit quality.

record.verdict_notes: The comparison value 0.24 mixes pretraining-loss exponents (Kaplan) with a math test-error exponent from an inference-scaling paper. It is a loose heuristic, not a matched comparison, so the 'universality' claim is unsupported by these data. The scaling experiment's model and number of runs per fraction are not stated.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits are used to predict much larger runs.
No compute-budget allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
Tests data scaling in financial fine-tuning only; does not test other modalities, repeated data, or transfer more broadly.
Tests performance scaling with fine-tuning data quantity on financial tasks, not scaling with model size or a relationship to pretraining loss.
Does not vary fitting choices or setup to test their effect on exponents or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned using varying fractions of aggregated available financial-task data and fitted a data-scaling relation.
rows.measure: Average F1 score; fitted scaling exponent for log(1−F1) against log(data fraction)
rows.value: Exponent 0.28; individual average F1 values are figure-only.
rows.locator: Section IV.d, Figure 2, and accompanying text
rows.note: The text reports the exponent as 0.28 and describes the measurement as a data scaling law. Figure 2 plots the average F1 results across fractions, but individual values are not stated numerically. Model identity is not given for this scaling experiment.
rows.check: The value should read: error (1−F1) falls with data fraction d, log(1−F1) ≈ −0.28·log(d) − 1.35. The minus signs are lost in extraction, but Fig. 2's axis (about 0.5 down to 0.2) confirms the decrease. The fit uses only 4 points over an 8× range, under one order of magnitude. The model is unidentified: only 1.5B models (DeepSeek-R1-1.5B / Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) are used elsewhere. No goodness of fit or uncertainty is given. Baseline is not applicable.
